data.title: Bangkok opens shelter for animals rescued from floodwaters
data.description: Dogs and cats displaced by severe flooding in Bangkok can now receive temporary shelter, health assessments and medical care at the Prawet Animal Shelter, the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) announced on Wednesday.

data.title: Bangkok's City Hall reported flooding on about 10 roads
data.description: The Drainage and Sewerage Department of the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) reported flooding on about 10 roads in the capital on Wednesday morning, with water levels ranging from seven to 20 centimetres.

data.title: Seed rights split growers from farmers
data.description: Thailand is preparing to discuss adopting UPOV 1991 with the European Union as part of free trade negotiations next month, with the proposed rules drawing support from seed producers but opposition from farmer groups concerned about restrictions on seed saving and exchange.

data.title: 13 more Chao Phraya piers go under contract
data.description: The Marine Department is pressing ahead with a 200-million-baht programme to develop 29 smart piers along the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok and surrounding areas, with all due to be completed by June 2028.

data.title: 4 NHA condo projects get nod
data.description: The government on Tuesday approved four apartment projects by the National Housing Authority (NHA), offering more opportunities for low-income people to access high-quality housing at a reasonable price.

data.title: Cops nab 2 for arson attack
data.description: Police have arrested a Turkish man, 31, and his ex-girlfriend, 40, a former sales manager, over an arson attack on a company in Bang Khae district of the capital.

data.title: PP demands QR codes off list ballots
data.description: People's Party (PP) list MP Parit Wacharasindhu has called for barcodes to be removed from party-list election ballots after the Constitutional Court ruled that their use was constitutional but warned that such markings could undermine public confidence in the secrecy of voting.

data.title: Huawei nabs 'excellence' gong
data.description: Huawei Thailand has won the Thailand Cybersecurity Excellence Awards 2026 in the Most Contribution category for the fifth consecutive year.

data.title: Thai envoy rebuts Cambodian claims
data.description: Thailand has accused Cambodia of making unfounded claims at the UN despite a ceasefire in place for more than nine months, and urged Phnom Penh to end border provocations and cooperate on security.

data.title: Red-shirt leaders walk free
data.description: Three red-shirt leaders have been granted amnesty for disrupting the 2009 Asean summit in Pattaya, with two released and the third's arrest warrant revoked.

data.title: Floods affect 2.6m with 22 deaths
data.description: Flooding in 29 provinces and Bangkok has affected more than 940,000 households and 2.6 million people, with 22 deaths reported as water levels continue to rise in several areas.

data.title: Polapee denies claim of meddling at reservoir
data.description: Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee denied ordering Khun Dan Prakan Chon Dam in Nakhon Nayok to stop releasing water, saying he merely asked whether releases could be slowed or temporarily halted to prevent downstream flooding.

data.title: Alarm bell sounds over new city plan
data.description: The Thailand Consumers Council has warned that Bangkok faces a growing risk of flooding from northern runoff, dam discharges, accumulated rainfall and high tides, and that a proposed new city plan could make matters worse by giving flood-retention areas over to housing estates and condominiums.

data.title: Anutin under fire over flooding
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul is facing public criticism over the government's response to flooding in and around Bangkok following three days of continuous rain.

data.title: Thai Airways cancels 37 more flights
data.description: Thai Airways International has cancelled 37 more domestic and international flights scheduled for Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday as it tries to dig itself out from under a massive baggage backlog at Suvarnabhumi airport.

data.title: Waterways overflow in northern Bangkok and nearby
data.description: People living near waterways in Nonthaburi and Pathum Thani provinces as well as adjacent districts of Bangkok have been warned to move belongings to higher ground as water levels are rising.

data.title: Owners warned, remove cars from bridges, elevated roads
data.description: Owners of vehicles left on bridges and elevated roads to escape floods in Bangkok are asked to quickly remove them as the water recedes and normal traffic resumes, in the interests of road safety.

data.title: US aircraft carrier with 5,000 crew to call on Phuket
data.description: USS George HW Bush the second large warship to visit Kingdom after Mideast duty

data.title: City Hall gears for flood clean-up
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) is preparing a major clean-up after the floodwaters recede, while urging residents to separate rubbish and securely bag infectious waste, sewage and food scraps, to prevent contamination.

data.title: Ratchaburi prepares for evacuations as Mae Klong River rises
data.description: Ratchaburi municipality on Tuesday alerted residents to be on standby for evacuation and ordered schools and childcare centres to close in the face of an imminent threat of major flooding from the rising Mae Klong River.

data.title: Nine drug smugglers killed in Chiang Rai shootout
data.description: Nine suspected drug smugglers were killed in an exchange of gunfire with security forces in a forested area in Mae Fa Luang district of Chiang Rai province on Monday night, with 272 kilogrammes of crystal methamphetamine seized.

data.title: Ratchaburi prepares to evacuate as Mae Klong River rises
data.description: Ratchaburi municipality on Tuesday alerted residents to be on standby for evacuation and ordered schools and childcare centres to close in the face of an imminent threat of major flooding from the rising Mae Klong River.

data.title: Cabinet approves B160bn flood mitigation project
data.description: Thailand’s Cabinet on Tuesday approved a 160-billion-baht project to divert water from Chai Nat through the Pasak River towards the Gulf of Thailand as a long-term solution to recurring flood problems in Bangkok and the central region.

data.title: Heavy rain closes 2 waterfalls in Chiang Mai
data.description: CHIANG MAI - Doi Suthep-Pui National Park closed access to two rain-swollen waterfalls on Tuesday as provincial authorities instructed local officials to remain vigilant for sudden natural hazards arising from heavy accumulated rainfall.

data.title: AI-based weather forecasting ‘still being studied’
data.description: The Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (DES) has denied reports about cabinet approval of a 497-million-baht project to introduce AI-powered weather forecasting from US-based Tomorrow.io to the Thai Meteorological Department.

data.title: Bangkok flood will drain off 'in a few days'
data.description: The flooding in eastern Bangkok will drain off in a few more days, provided it does not rain again, government spokesman Ekkapob Pianpises said on Tuesday.

data.title: 5,600 delayed bags, 330 stalled flights prompt THAI apology
data.description: The torrential rain and flooding in Bangkok over the weekend led to long delays in handling about 5,600 bags and 330 stalled Thai Airways International flights, after hundreds of airline workers were stranded at home, unable to go to work at the capital's two international airports.
